tagline: From Grand Oaks to Texas' all-time list.
headline: Texas Track & Field · Pole Vault

school.name: The University of Texas at Austin

bio.short: Sophia Kowalski is a senior pole vaulter for Texas Track & Field whose 4.17m clearance in 2025 ranked No. 6 on the Longhorns' all-time list. A two-time USTFCCCA All-Academic honoree studying Nutrition, she was a 2026 Project Manager Intern at Feniex Industries.
long: Sophia Kowalski has vaulted for the University of Texas since 2023 and is a senior in 2026-27. As a freshman she cleared 4.15m (13-7.25) for second at the Texas Invitational, moving onto the Longhorns' all-time performer list, and reached the NCAA West First Round. In February 2025 she cleared a career-best 4.17m (13-8.25) at the New Mexico Collegiate Classic to move to No. 6 all-time. She has competed at two SEC Indoor Championships, won the 2025 Dr. MLK Jr. Invitational and finished runner-up at the 2026 Leonard Hilton Memorial and UTSA Invitational.

She is from Spring, Texas, north of Houston, and left Grand Oaks High School as its pole vault record holder after placing fourth at the 2023 UIL State Championships with a clearance of 13-0. She also competed for MAC Vault Academy, a specialist pole vault club, and was a member of the National Honor Society. At Texas she majors in Nutrition and was named to both the USTFCCCA All-Academic Team and the SEC Academic Honor Roll in 2025 and 2026. She credits her father with her success in the sport.

In 2026 she joined Feniex Industries, the Austin manufacturer of emergency-vehicle lighting and sirens, as a Project Manager Intern. Pole vault is a technical event run on preparation: steps, grip, pole and bar height all have to line up before a single attempt, and there are only three tries at each height. That habit of checking every detail, adjusting between attempts and staying calm when the margin is small carries straight into coordinating schedules, documentation and handoffs between teams.
